test_title: PYST 02: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He asked me affectionately what he could do for me.

options.text: He said to me, "What can be done for me?"
He said to me, "What could he do?"
He said to me, "What should be done for you?"
He said to me, "What can I do for you, dear?".

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He asked me affectionately what he could do for me.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"what he could do for me" becomes "What can I do for you"**
 
 
• Indirect question "what he could do" is converted to direct question "What can I do".
 
• Pronoun "he" is changed to "I" to match direct speech.
 
• Pronoun "me" is changed to "you" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "could" is changed to "can" to match the present tense in direct questions.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "He asked me affectionately"
 
• Converted to: "He said to me, dear" maintaining the affectionate tone.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "What" and ends with a question mark "?".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“What can I do for you, dear?” he said to me"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He said to me, "What can be done for me?" 

 
 
• Changes the meaning to imply that the speaker is asking what can be done for himself, not the listener.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He said to me, "What could he do?"" 
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun usage and changes the meaning to a general question without the affectionate tone.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said to me, "What should be done for you?"" 
 
 
• Changes the verb to "should" and loses the affectionate tone.
